title: The Moon between the Star and the Sun

article.title: The Moon between the Star and the Sun
article.lead: In the matrix of your couple the lower corners hold Stars, the centre holds the Moon and the upper corners hold the Sun: three luminaries of the Tarot lined up on the scheme from bottom to top. You live by moonlight — you understand each other from reflections, without words, and that is your closeness. The main task is to turn guesses into things said and agreed, so that silence stays a rest and doesn’t become a wall. Below, “the September one” is whichever of you was born on 5 September 1990, and “the February one” is whoever was born on 21 February 1987. This is a symbolic reading for a couple’s self-knowledge, not a forecast and not a psychological diagnosis.
summary: **You are a sensitive and quiet couple, and these qualities feed each other.** The Moon stands in the centre, the Hermit in the task, the common language and the values; the repeats add up in a circle: 9 + 9 = 18, 18 + 18 = 9. One partner’s silence turns into the other’s guesses.

**Your tool is an honest agreement.** Justice appears five times, from the image to the crossing of money and relationships: according to the book it means keeping accounts, a plan B and one’s word; the cost is a silent tally of contributions.

**One and the same Sun both fills you and makes you quarrel.** Both upper corners are the Sun, though they are added up from different points of yours; two Suns together give Strength (19 + 19 = 11) — the point you met for.
**Money comes through talent, prosperity through change.** At the entry to money stands the Star, in the point of prosperity the Tower, which neither of you has on your own.
**By the book’s standards your characters are compatible.** You both have the Fool as your dual, and one partner’s desires in relationships are the other’s spiritual purpose, crosswise.
**Order helps you make peace.** You both have the Emperor as your point of reconciliation; together it is Justice in the point “what connects you”: a quarrel ends with an agreement.

chapters.h2: The key of the couple: living by moonlight and stepping into the light
chapters.conclusion: Your couple rests on wordless sensitivity and on each partner’s right to be alone for a while. In difficult times the same qualities turn into silence and guesses. The main idea of the report: what you sense about each other needs to be said out loud and turned into an agreement — gently and honestly.

cards.label: Atmosphere of the couple
cards.caption: The large circle in the centre is what is between you and not on show. The Moon: sensitivity, half-tones, understanding without words, and guesses.

blocks: If you look at the scheme of your couple from bottom to top, you can see a sky on it. In both lower corners — the Star, in the centre — the Moon, in both upper corners — the Sun. In the Tarot deck these three cards come in a row, 17, 18 and 19, and on your scheme they stand in the same order, from the lower edge to the upper one. This is not a law of how the scheme is built but a property of your two dates in particular, and it describes precisely how your couple lives.

formula.caption: **17, 18, 19.** The Star, the Moon and the Sun stand on the couple’s scheme from bottom to top in the order they come in the deck. In a couple the lower corners are amplifiers, the centre is the atmosphere of the couple, and the upper corners are what fills the union and what can spoil it.

blocks.h3: Reflected light

blocks: Waite, describing the Moon and the Sun, contrasts them as two kinds of light. The Moon shines with reflected light: by it you can see outlines but not everything, and the imagination draws in the rest. The Sun is direct light: by it things are seen as they are. Your shared atmosphere is the Moon. You understand each other from reflections: from the pause before an answer, from the way the other closed their laptop, from a too-even “everything’s fine”. This is real closeness, and many couples don’t reach it in years. For Lisovskaya the Moon in the atmosphere means high sensitivity, a partner who is above all a friend, respect for personal space, understanding without words; over time such a couple grows together and every year discovers something new in each other.

But reflected light is deceptive. In the half-dark a familiar armchair is easily mistaken for a stranger’s figure, and a partner’s tiredness for a grievance against you. Among the Moon’s minuses the book lists grievances from made-up stories, disappointments over trifles and quarrels out of nowhere. It is the same sensitivity, only aimed at your own guesses instead of the living person beside you.

blocks.h3: Three Hermits

blocks: The couple’s second main card is the Hermit, and it stands three times. In the main task (the large circle at the bottom). At the entry to the task, where the book places the couple’s shared desires, its agreements and its “common language” (the inner circle below the centre). And in the spiritual purpose — the values of the couple. You both need silence, time of your own, a deep conversation instead of chatter, the right to think first and answer later. In the Hermit’s plus each has their own place to be alone, love is shown through actions, agreements are trusted. In the task the same energy reads in the minus: in difficult times each hides in their own shell, and problems pile up in silence.

blocks.h3: The loop: silence breeds guesses, guesses breed silence

blocks: Lisovskaya advises adding up a couple’s repeated energies: if the sum also stands in the matrix, it sounds at full strength. In your case this arithmetic closes into a circle.

formula.caption: **9 + 9 = 18.** Two silences together give the Moon. When both withdraw into themselves, the space for guesses between you grows.
**18 + 18 = 36 → 9.** Two Moons together give the Hermit. The more that is unclear between you, the stronger the pull to fall silent and figure it out alone.

blocks: Lisovskaya analyses this link in her book on the couple Maria and Alexei. Their nines also add up to 18, but there is no eighteen in their shared matrix, and the author reads it as a faint trail: too much fantasy and an image of the partner give false hopes, and when they collapse, the person shuts down and, in her words, “torments the partner with their reticence”. In your case the same sum does not remain a trail: the Moon stands in the very centre of the couple. What sounds as background for Maria and Alexei is your shared atmosphere.

This is what the main mechanism of your couple looks like. One partner is tired and has withdrawn — that is the Hermit, and there is nothing wrong with it. The other sees a closed door and starts guessing what is behind it: a grievance? disappointment? irritation with them? That is the Moon. So as not to be wrong and not to impose, the second partner also falls silent and waits — the Hermit again. Now two people are silently drawing each other in. Two days later both sincerely believe the other was the first to pull away. Nobody did anything wrong, and yet there is a chill.

The circle can be broken at any point, and always in the same way: with words. Withdrawing becomes safe when it is named: “I need an evening of quiet, we’re fine.” A guess loses its power when it has been checked with a question: “I had the feeling you were upset with me — is that so?” This way out has a support in the matrix, and it stands at the top.

blocks.h3: What you met for

blocks: Lisovskaya reads what a couple met for from the large circle at the top — only in its plus — together with the large circle on the left: the pluses of the two energies weave into the meaning of the meeting, the minuses into the couple’s earthly trials. At the top you have Strength, on the left Justice. Justice gives measure: what is fair, what was said, what was promised. In Waite, Strength is a woman who holds a lion with a chain of flowers: firmness without roughness, courage without pressure. Together it is the ability to tell the truth in a way that can be heard.

The Strength in the meeting point is added up from two quiet talents of yours — the September one’s Hermit and the February one’s High Priestess; more on this in the chapter on what each brings to the couple. Quiet plus quiet produced an energy that comes outward, and that says a lot about the meaning of your meeting.

For a couple with the Moon in the centre and the Hermit at the bottom, such a meeting means a lot. You met to learn to bring into the light what lives in the half-dark: to name what you are silent about, to agree on what each understood in their own way, and to do it with care. Your shared work is gentle clarity. Ruthless truth won’t replace it, and neither will polite silence.

The bond of Strength and Justice also has a trial, and a quiet couple has its own. Here truth is more often hoarded than imposed: you keep quiet until a lot has piled up, and then lay it all out at once and firmly, with the gentleness gone. Waite’s Strength holds the lion with a chain of flowers, and for you this is advice about the dose: speak a little at a time and on time, while the truth can still be carried gently.

blocks.h3: Values of the couple

blocks: The couple’s spiritual purpose is the Hermit again. Lisovskaya reads it on its own and together with the upper corners, the atmosphere, the image and the meeting point. Your values are meaning, depth, a path of your own to understanding. The atmosphere — the Moon — gives this path sensitivity, Justice in the image gives honesty, Strength in the meeting point gives courage. The Sun in both upper corners reminds you: a couple lives the Hermit’s values in the light, in shared experiences, activities and pride in each other. A couple that only understands silently eventually stops understanding.

blocks.h3: Your couple in one evening

blocks: Here is an evening in which your whole matrix can be seen. You are both at home, each busy with your own thing, and you feel good — that is the Hermit in the common language. One of you goes quiet a little differently than usual, and the other notices it before they have time to think — the Moon in the centre. They ask, and the conversation runs past midnight: one tells an unpleasant truth gently, the other takes it without offence — Strength and Justice, which you met for. In the morning there is an agreement on how to go on, and both feel calm — the Emperor in each one’s point of reconciliation. And at the weekend you go somewhere you have never been and come back feeling that you see each other clearly again — the Sun that fills you.

Hence one idea all the chapters converge on. **In your couple one partner’s silence turns into the other’s guesses by itself — that is how your numbers add up, and intuition alone is not enough against it. Your support is different: five Justices and Strength in the meeting point. Bring what you sense about each other and about your life to an agreement — a gentle but clear one.** Your money, your household, your quarrels and your care are all arranged by this rule.

actions: Agree on a signal phrase for withdrawing, for example “I need some quiet, we’re fine”, and say it every time you feel like closing off.
For a week, check every anxious guess about your partner with one direct question before reacting to it.
Once a week hold an evening when each tells what they have understood about the other over these days, and the other confirms or corrects it.

chapters.h2: What the automatic reading does not show
chapters.conclusion: Eight links that cannot be seen if the points are read one by one: one Sun from two different sources, the sum of two Suns, a shared point of reconciliation, an identical crossing of money and relationships, a cross of desires and purposes, the Lovers, who are not in the couple but are in each of you, your signs in the Tarot, and which of you knows which theme of the couple from the inside.

cards.caption: Justice: the image, the material, parents in tandem, what connects you, the crossing of money and relationships.

cards.label: New to both of you

finding.title: One Sun in both upper corners — from different points of yours

formula.caption: **19 ↔ 19.** The couple’s symmetrical upper corners are held by one card, though they add up from different points of yours: the left one from your points of inspiration (14 + 5), the right one from your triggers (10 + 9).

text: Each point of a couple is the sum of the two partners’ points of the same name. The upper left corner, which for Lisovskaya is responsible for what fills the union, is added up from your personal points of inspiration: the September one’s Temperance and the February one’s Hierophant, 14 + 5 = 19. The upper right corner, what can spoil the union, comes from your triggers, the points through which each of you is easiest to hurt: the September one’s Wheel and the February one’s Hermit, 10 + 9 = 19. Two independent sums gave one card.

The meaning of the coincidence is simple and important: what inspires you and what hurts you meet in one energy. The Sun is your fuel and your main reason for quarrels, and the boundary between them runs along one question: is it shining for each of you? What this looks like at home and by what signs to notice a shift into the minus — in the chapter on what fills you.

Your side circles also coincide, and that is a separate coincidence: both the image of the couple and the material point hold Justice. The image is how people see the couple; the material point is its household, spending, savings and, according to Lisovskaya, also physical intimacy. How you look and how you live in material terms are one and the same. You have no gap between the shop window and the kitchen, while many couples do: generous outside, counting every trifle at home, or the other way round.
finding.action: Mark both partners’ successes in a shared calendar. If after a month only one name has collected there, it is a sign the Sun is shining for one, and it is time to find a reason to shine for the other.

finding.title: Two Suns add up to Strength — the very one you met for

formula.caption: **19 + 19 = 38 → 11.** The sum of the two Suns stands in the couple’s matrix twice: in the meeting point and below it, on the talent line.

text: Repeats, as a reminder, are added up, and if the sum is in the matrix, it works at full strength. Your two Suns give Strength — the very one that, according to the book, you met for. This answers the question from the previous finding: what to do with a Sun that both fills you and makes you quarrel. The light doesn’t need to be divided by working out who shines brighter. It needs to be added up.

Strength in a couple means two people who charge and reinforce each other, sense finely what the partner needs, and know how to give way and find a compromise. When two ambitions look in the same direction, the result is an endurance neither has on their own. When they look at each other, Strength does not add up: two separate ambitions remain.

One of you is preparing for an important interview or talk, and the other becomes the coach: drills the questions, listens to the rehearsal, takes over all the housework on the day. Six months later the roles switch. Each time the light is on one, and the credit is shared — that is how two Suns add up to Strength.
finding.action: Choose one goal where one partner’s success will be both partners’ success, and assign the roles: who leads, who covers the rear; in three months swap.

finding.title: Five Justices lead back to the Emperor — the point of reconciliation for you both

formula.caption: **4 + 4 = 8.** In each of your personal matrices the point through which you can make peace with the person is the Emperor. In the couple’s matrix these two points add up to Justice in the point “what connects you”.

text: Justice stands in the couple’s matrix five times. Let’s add up the repeats, as Lisovskaya advises: 8 × 5 = 40, 4 + 0 = 4 — the Emperor. There is no Emperor in the couple’s matrix, and according to the book such a sum sounds weakly, as a trail. But it stands in your personal matrices, for both of you in the very same point — the middle of the relationship line. In her book for beginners Lisovskaya calls it the point of relationships: through what you can make peace with a person and find a common language.

So the same thing calms you both — order. A clear plan, a clear “who does what”, a decision that has been made and said out loud. After a quarrel it is not enough for you to hug and say “oh well”. You need to understand how things will go from here: “I won’t stay late again without calling”, “on Saturdays we clean together, then we’re free”. Until that “from here” exists, peace feels temporary.

Your two points of reconciliation add up in the couple’s matrix to Justice in the point “what connects you”. The result is a ready formula: two people calmed by order are connected through an honest agreement. And the good news: you have no clash of reconciliation styles. The same conversation suits you both — the one that ends with a concrete decision.

There is a subtlety too. The Emperor in the minus is rigid rules, control, decisions made for everyone. If there are too many agreements, order starts to suffocate, and every deviation becomes a violation. A rule is needed as long as it helps you both live more calmly.
finding.action: End every relationship showdown with one concrete agreement for the coming week — said out loud and clear to both.

finding.title: An identical crossing of money and relationships — and a Tower that neither of you has

formula.caption: **8 + 8 = 16.** The middle of the money line is Justice for both of you. In the couple’s matrix it doubles into the Tower, which stands in the point of prosperity.

text: In the lower right sector of a personal matrix money and relationships meet: the middle of the money line, the middle of the relationship line and the point where they cross. For both of you these three points are the same: 8, 4 and 22. Earnings through Justice, reconciliation through the Emperor, the dual is the Fool. In money and relationships you are built alike: both of you earn through clear, honest work, by agreement, both are calmed by order, both need freedom.

Matching duals in themselves speak of compatible characters: according to the book, when one person’s dual energy stands in a suitable point of the other’s matrix, people understand each other without explanations. What is new here is something else. Your two Justices of earnings add up in the couple to the Tower, and neither of you has the Tower in your personal matrix. Lisovskaya analyses a similar case in her book: if the partners don’t have an energy, the couple lives this experience for the first time and together.

Your couple’s prosperity will come through something you don’t do separately: through rebuilding. The Tower in finances in the plus is a shared budget and big shared investments, building or renovating together, discipline by rules invented together. Each of you knows how to earn honestly on your own. Together you have to learn to dare big changes: a move, a shared project, a change of lifestyle. The Tower’s minuses in money are sudden changes in income, fear of change, a habit of expecting the worst, and different views of money because of different levels of wealth in your parents’ families.

The duals add up the same way: 22 + 22 = 44 → 8. At the crossing of money and relationships in the couple’s matrix there is Justice again. Two freedoms together give the couple a rule: each one’s freedom rests on an honest agreement.
finding.action: Set up a separate “rebuilding” fund and agree what big change you are saving for and what the first step towards it will be this year.

finding.title: One partner’s desires are the other’s path, crosswise

formula.caption: **18 = 18.** What the September one wants from relationships is the Moon; the February one’s spiritual purpose is also the Moon. From the other side the picture is the same: the February one’s desires and the September one’s path are the Hermit.

text: A personal matrix has a half-dual point — the inner circle below the centre, the start of the relationship line. Lisovskaya writes that it shows what a person wants from relationships and through which energy they look at others. The September one has the Moon here, the February one the Hermit. Now the spiritual purposes: the September one has the Hermit, the February one the Moon. Crosswise: what one seeks in closeness is the other’s road in life. And the February one’s Hermit also stands in the September one’s matrix in the place of the main talent.

According to the book for beginners, a half-dual energy found in the other person’s spiritual path or main talent speaks of compatibility. At the same time a half-dual, by her definition, is a person with whom you have many points of contact but some topics the two of you understand differently, as if in different languages, and there you have to learn to get your meaning across.

This is where those different languages lie for you. In closeness the September one needs the Moon: understanding without words, mystery, the feeling of being guessed. The February one needs the Hermit: silence, a space of one’s own, the right to think. Both get this from the partner, but in someone else’s rendering. The February one, respecting space, doesn’t press with questions, and the September one may read this as inattention. The September one expects to be sensed without words, and the February one may take this as an exam for which they were given no questions.

The good side of the cross is that each can learn their own desire from the other. The February one, for whom the Moon is a path, knows its subtleties better than many and can give the September one the wordless closeness they seek. The September one, for whom the Hermit is a path and a talent, can show the February one how solitude makes a person deeper without leading them away from the people close to them.
finding.action: Each of you finish the sentence “I feel you’ve understood me when you…” with three concrete examples, and swap sheets.

finding.title: The Lovers: a counterweight to the Moon that the couple lacks but each of you has

formula.caption: **17 + 17 + 17 = 51 → 6.** The couple’s three Stars add up to the Lovers. There is no six in the couple’s matrix, so according to the book it sounds weakly, as a trail. But it is in each of your personal matrices.

text: The February one has the Lovers in the centre of their personal matrix, the September one in the karmic task. The couple’s matrix doesn’t have them: your shared atmosphere is the Moon. This matters, because for Lisovskaya the Lovers in a couple are an almost exact opposite of the lunar half-dark: sincerity, no secrets, lots of touch, talking about everything, deciding together even on trifles.

So what the couple lacks most, each of you carries inside, but it doesn’t pass into the shared atmosphere by itself. It has to be brought in consciously. It is easier for the February one: openness of feeling and a pull towards agreement are part of their own centre. It is harder for the September one: in their personal matrix the Lovers are a task, something they learn all their life. The couple is a good place to work through it, and next to them is someone for whom it comes naturally.

In practice these are small things. A touch in passing when you walk past each other in the kitchen. The word “love” for no reason. Deciding a trifle together — which bread to buy, where to hang a shelf. A compliment said rather than thought. Separately it is nothing, but it is exactly from such nothings that an atmosphere with less room for guesses is built. Let the February one set the tone and the September one pick it up.
finding.action: For a week, every day do one such small thing — a touch, a word of tenderness, a shared decision about a trifle — and at the end of the week discuss whether anything has changed at home.

finding.title: Your signs in the Tarot are the two main cards of the couple
text: This is a different system, not the matrix method, and we give it as a separate observation. In the Western Tarot tradition — in the Golden Dawn correspondences, which Benebell Wen also uses in “Holistic Tarot” — each zodiac sign has its own card. Virgo, to which 5 September belongs, corresponds to the Hermit: Wen writes directly that this card can point to the sign of Virgo and the period from 23 August to 22 September. Pisces, to which 21 February belongs, corresponds to the Moon, the period from 19 February to 20 March.

The two cards of your signs are the two main cards of your couple: the Hermit in the task, the common language and the values, the Moon in the atmosphere and the middle of the tasks. More than that, for each of you the card of the sign coincides with your own spiritual purpose by the matrix: for the September one it is the Hermit, for the February one the Moon. Two independent systems show the same thing: each brings their own card into the couple, and the couple is built on their meeting.

This is no proof: the calculation of the matrix does not depend on the zodiac. But it lets your couple be described in words that make sense without a scheme. One is the one who looks inward, seeks meaning and is in no hurry. The other is the one with strong intuition who lives in half-tones, in a constant change of moods. If people close to you ask what your couple is about, you can answer like this.
finding.action: Each of you choose from the two cards, the Hermit and the Moon, the one that describes your partner more accurately, and compare answers: whether it matches the matrix or not, it is a good reason to talk.

finding.title: Each theme of the couple is already known from the inside by one of you
text: Lisovskaya advises looking for a couple’s repeated energies in the personal matrices: that shows which of the two knows the theme from their own life. It is a resource, not a fault. The one who has the energy knows both its strength and its cost better, and it is easier for them to be the first to notice that the couple is sliding into the minus.

The Hermit is shared, and this is the main thing: both understand silence and depth. The Moon is what the September one seeks in closeness and what the February one lives as a path. Justice stands in both partners’ earnings, and for the February one also among the talents — it is easier for them to turn agreements into working rules. The Star, Strength and the Sun are brought by the September one: they have the Star in the parents’ point, Strength in a lower corner, the Sun in the material point. Both know the Chariot: the February one has it in the material point, the September one in a lower corner. Death, which stands on the couple’s talent line, is the February one’s entry to money. Nobody has the Tower, through which prosperity comes.

A practical conclusion. When the couple argues over successes and comparisons, it is easier for the September one to stop first: they know the Sun from the inside. When feelings need to be turned into an agreement, it is easier for the February one to lead. When the couple needs a dream and inspiration for money, the September one brings them. When you need to dare a change, the February one’s Death at the entry to money will come in handy — the ability to finish the old and start anew.

chapters.conclusion: Your main personal energies hardly pass into the couple’s matrix as they are: they add up into new ones. The centres give the Moon, the masks Justice, the main talents Strength, the duals Justice again. You complement each other through your masks and talents and clash through your centres: what is natural for one is a personal lesson for the other.

blocks.h3: Centres: wait or choose

formula.caption: **12 + 6 = 18.** The couple’s atmosphere is added up from your personal centres — the points where each of you feels calm and natural.

blocks: The centre of a personal matrix is who a person is when no one is getting in their way. The September one has the Hanged Man there: the ability to stop, to wait, to look at a situation from an unexpected angle, to give up the momentary for the sake of meaning. The February one has the Lovers: choosing with the heart, open feelings, a need for agreement and warmth nearby. Together these two energies give the Moon, and it is clear why: one is in no hurry for certainty, the other seeks it in feelings, and a space of half-tones remains between them.

In everyday life this shows at every step. A question comes up — where to go in the summer, whether to change flats, whether to go to old friends’ birthday party. For the February one it matters to choose and to feel that the choice is shared: “let’s decide — are you with me?” For the September one it is natural to wait: “let’s see nearer the time, maybe everything will change”. For one, waiting is wisdom; for the other, it is a suspension in which it is unclear whether you are together. Neither is more right than the other. But if such questions hang for weeks, the Moon in the couple’s centre fills up with versions: “doesn’t want to go with me?”, “again everything has to be decided right now?”

For the dual Lisovskaya gives a rule: if one person’s energy stands in the other’s trigger, material karma or karmic tail, it is a point of conflict — the energy is good for one, while the other has misunderstandings around it. The same view is useful for the centres too, and for you it holds for both. The September one’s Hanged Man stands in the middle of the February one’s personal karmic tail. The February one’s Lovers are the September one’s karmic task. What is natural for one is a lesson that comes hard to the other. A calm “let’s wait” touches in the February one a theme they are working through in themselves. An open “let’s choose, let’s feel it” asks of the September one what they are learning all their life.

The same bond is the best textbook for both. Next to the September one, the February one can learn to wait without anxiety; next to the February one, the September one can learn to choose with the heart and talk about feelings. A simple rule for open questions helps: the one who wants to wait names how long, and after that deadline a decision is made without fail. “We wait until Friday, then we decide” suits both centres at once.

blocks.h3: Masks: each looks like what the other needs

formula.caption: **5 + 21 = 26 → 8.** The image of the couple is added up from your personal masks — how each of you appears to people.

blocks: The September one has the Hierophant in the point of the mask: seriousness, reliance on rules and knowledge, a manner of explaining. The February one has the World: breadth, openness, the ability to feel at home in any setting. Together they give the image of the couple — Justice: one brings solidity, the other breadth, and people see two people with everything in balance.

More interesting is where one partner’s mask stands in the other’s matrix. The September one’s Hierophant in the February one’s personal matrix is the point of inspiration. The February one’s World is the September one’s additional talent. Each looks on the outside like what the other has inside: the September one shows the world what inspires the February one, and the February one shows what the September one has as a hidden talent. Perhaps that is where your first attraction came from: in the other you saw something of your own, only expressed.

In company this is noticeable: it is easier for the February one to strike up a conversation with strangers, and for the September one to bring it to the point. In public you are a good team, as long as each does their own part and nobody tries to play someone else’s role.

blocks.h3: Main talents: two quiet gifts add up to strength

formula.caption: **9 + 2 = 11.** The couple’s meeting point is added up from your main talents: the Hermit and the High Priestess.

blocks: The September one’s main talent is the Hermit: thinking deeply and independently, getting to the essence. The February one’s main talent is the High Priestess: hearing the unspoken, understanding through half-tones, keeping what was entrusted. Both talents are quiet, both are about the inner world. Together they give Strength — an energy that comes outward. Separately each of you knows how to understand. Together you can also learn to act on that understanding, gently and firmly.

The September one’s matrix has no High Priestess at all, and it doesn’t pass into the couple’s matrix as it is. It is something new the February one brings: the ability to notice what is hidden in people and to keep other people’s secrets. For the September one this may be one of the reasons it feels calm next to this person: they are understood more deeply than they explain.

The September one’s Hermit, on the contrary, appears in the February one’s matrix three times: in the desires from relationships, in the parents’ point and in the trigger — the point through which a person is easiest to influence. For the February one, the September one’s depth and independence are both attractive and sensitive: this is exactly what they want from closeness, and exactly what hurts them most easily. When the September one withdraws into their thoughts, the February one values it as intelligence and depth. But if the withdrawal drags on or comes at a bad moment, they take it closer to heart than it looks from the outside.

blocks.h3: Duals: one freedom for two

formula.caption: **22 + 22 = 44 → 8.** Two freedoms together give the couple Justice at the crossing of money and relationships.

blocks: You both have the Fool as your dual, and for each it stands in the same point in the other’s matrix, at the crossing of money and relationships. The September one also has the Fool in the children’s point. According to Lisovskaya, when the dual matches a suitable point in the partner’s matrix, it speaks of compatible characters: you understand each other in the main thing — the need for freedom, lightness and the right to start over. In the couple two freedoms add up to Justice: your freedom rests on an agreement. How to arrange this in practice — in the chapter on relationships.

blocks.h3: Spiritual purposes: one partner’s path became the couple’s path

blocks: The last thing Lisovskaya advises writing out for each person is the spiritual purpose. For the September one it is the Hermit, for the February one the Moon, for the couple the Hermit again. The September one’s path coincided with the couple’s path: depth, meaning, a way of one’s own to understand the world. The February one’s path became the couple’s atmosphere: the sensitivity and half-tones you live in every day. So the values of your union are closer to the September one, and its air to the February one. For both this is a resource: it is easier for the September one to keep the couple’s course on meaning, and for the February one to sense when something has shifted in the atmosphere.

blocks.h3: What it looks like in one shared task

blocks: Say you are choosing where to go on holiday. The February one, with the World as mask, finds options, writes to people who have been there, easily agrees with the hosts. The September one, with the Hierophant as mask, checks reliability: reviews, terms, a backup plan. The February one’s High Priestess notices what the September one didn’t say: that they really want quiet, not a packed programme. The September one’s Hermit thinks the trip through to the end and finds meaning in it — a place they have long wanted to learn more about. If at the same time the September one doesn’t drag out the decision too long and the February one doesn’t demand an answer that same evening, you get a holiday that suits both and that you remember for a long time. All four points show here at once: the masks assigned the roles, the talents added depth, the centres set the pace, and an agreed deadline removed the clash.

blocks.h3: What each can learn from the other

blocks: If you look at your personal matrices side by side, each has something the other lacks as a skill, and this is a ready-made programme of learning from each other.

ul: **The September one from the February one** — choosing with the heart and talking about feelings (the Lovers in the February one’s centre are the September one’s karmic task) and hearing the unspoken (the September one has no High Priestess at all). An exercise: once a week the September one is the first to name one of their feelings and one decision they want to make together.

**The February one from the September one** — waiting without anxiety (the Hanged Man in the September one’s centre stands in the February one’s personal tail) and withdrawing without guilt (the September one’s Hermit is their main talent). An exercise: next time an open question hangs, the February one suggests a waiting period themselves and keeps to it.
**Both from each other** — freedom by agreement. You share a dual, and each can show the other how to be free without worrying the partner: in advance, clearly, with a story afterwards.

blocks.h3: Where you complement each other and where you clash

blocks: You complement each other:

ul: **through the mask and inspiration** — each shows the world what the other has inside: the September one’s Hierophant inspires the February one, the February one’s World is the September one’s hidden talent;
**through talents** — the Hermit’s depth and the High Priestess’s sensitivity together give Strength, which you met for;
**through duals** — the same need for freedom, so the very principle of freedom is not disputed between you;
**through desires and purposes** — the cross of half-duals from the findings: what one seeks in closeness is the other’s path.

blocks: You clash:

ul: **through centres** — the Hanged Man and the Lovers stand in each other’s karmic tails: “let’s wait” against “let’s decide”;
**through the Hermit on the trigger** — the September one’s withdrawal hurts the February one more than it looks from the outside.

blocks: None of these clashes makes either of you a difficult partner. They are places where your natural energies need translating: what is simply character for one is a theme the other is working on in themselves. Knowing this, it is easier not to take the other’s nature as an attitude towards yourself.
actions: For every open question, let the one who wants to wait name the waiting period; after it a decision is made without fail.
Tell each other what once attracted you in the other, and check it against the masks in the table: often what attracts us is our own, only expressed.

To the September one: when withdrawing into your thoughts for a long time, give a warning — for the February one this is a sensitive point. To the February one: remember that this depth is exactly what you wanted from closeness.

chapters.h2: The couple outside and inside: a clear façade and a room in half-tones
chapters.conclusion: On the outside you look like a composed, reliable and restrained couple that keeps its word. Inside there are more half-tones than can be seen from the outside: sensitivity, changes of mood, things left unsaid. Both are worth looking after, and the gap between them is worth watching.

cards.label: Image of the couple
cards.caption: The large circle on the left is how people see you. Justice: order, directness, promises that are kept.

cards.label: Atmosphere
cards.caption: The large circle in the centre is what is really between you. The Moon: sensitivity, intuition, half-tones.

blocks.h3: How you are seen

blocks: Lisovskaya describes Justice in the image of a couple like this: a conservative, organised, pragmatic couple without much spontaneity. Direct, restrained in public, but with love and passion. They looked each other over for a long time and took a long time to adjust to each other — and you can see it in how calmly they carry themselves now.

If your couple lives in the plus of this energy, people see two people they can rely on. Ask you to help with a move and you will arrive at nine, as agreed, with gloves and tape. Acquaintances come to you to settle a dispute, because you don’t play along with whoever is louder. You will rarely be called the most romantic couple in the group and almost always the most reliable. That the same Justice also stands in your material point is covered in the findings: as you look, so you live.

This image has a recognisable minus too. Directness in public sometimes backfires: one honestly corrects the other at the table — “not in 2019 but in 2020, and not in Sochi but in Adler” — and from the outside it looks like a small public exam. Among the minuses of Justice in the image, the book names a habit of exposing the partner’s shortcomings and a feeling that the two live like neighbours. Neither says anything about feelings. It is just that justice brought out in front of guests reads to others as coldness.

blocks.h3: What is inside

blocks: Inside you have the Moon. It is an atmosphere only the two of you can see. A fine tuning to each other: you notice a change of mood before the person has realised it themselves. A world of fantasies, shared jokes only the two of you understand, a habit of exchanging a look instead of a sentence. In the Moon’s plus the partner is above all a friend, personal space is respected, and over time the couple grows together and stands up for each other like a wall.

What this Moon is made of — the September one’s Hanged Man and the February one’s Lovers — and why one of you tends to wait in it and the other to choose is covered in the chapter on what each brings to the couple.

The Moon’s minus inside is unclarity that piles up. The mood changes, but the reason isn’t named. Hurt arises over what the other “should have sensed”. The book warns of disappointments over trifles and that a partner’s secrets can become a weapon in a quarrel. Lisovskaya also advises not speaking badly of your partner, believing that with this energy what is said comes true especially easily. That is her belief, but its practical meaning is clear: in a couple where everything is felt, a hurtful word sticks for a long time.

blocks.h3: The gap between the façade and the room

blocks: The most interesting thing about your couple is the distance between the image and the atmosphere. Outside is Justice: clarity, rules, everything named. Inside is the Moon: half-tones, and much is not named. Perhaps order on the outside is what helps you bear unclarity inside. When everything in feelings is shaky, it is nice to know that at least the bills are paid and the weekend plans are set.

The danger is that the façade starts to replace conversation. Everything looks right — things are done, promises kept — and so it seems there is nothing to talk about. And inside, the unspoken lives for weeks. Friends would be surprised to learn that such a clear couple has days when the two don’t understand each other. Sometimes you are surprised yourselves.

You have a way back too: the same Justice can be turned inward. Let clarity work not only for guests and bills but for feelings too. “I’m sad today, and it’s not because of you” is as honest an agreement as “you pay for electricity, I pay for the internet”. Justice knows how to call things by their names — exactly what the Moon lacks.

blocks.h3: At home, visiting, in conflict

ul: **At home.** Each of you can do your own thing in the same room — one reading, the other watching something with headphones — and it is rest. You sense each other even without talking. A worrying sign is when you spend the evening side by side but learn each other’s news from your phones.

**Visiting.** You keep an even, polite manner, listen well, are unlikely to be the life of the party, but people talk to you about important things. You come home with impressions that you discuss on the way, and for you that is the best part of the evening. A worrying sign is one of you correcting or judging the other in public.

**In conflict.** You argue about facts and get hurt by tone. Justice keeps the conversation within limits — what happened, who promised what — while the Moon remembers the voice it was said in. So a quarrel can formally end with the right decision and remain inside as an unspoken hurt. After an argument it helps to ask a separate question: “We’ve agreed on the matter. But how did the way I spoke feel to you?”

blocks.h3: What the people close to you see and don’t see

blocks: The people close to you see Justice in you — a couple where everything is fair. If that is how it is for you, your relatives feel calm with you, while friends sometimes don’t understand what is going on between you: you don’t take quarrels outside, and you don’t display tenderness. Some will decide everything is even with you and therefore boring, others that you are hiding something. In fact the Moon simply keeps the main things inside.

This point has one request for you. Justice in the image is honest, which means that with the people close to you, you can also talk honestly about difficulties when you need help. A couple with Justice in its image tends to keep up appearances to the last: “we’re fine”, when in fact it is hard. Asking for advice or support is also part of honesty, and it doesn’t make either of you weak.

blocks.h3: Which couples to be friends with

blocks: The image of the couple also suggests whom you are at ease with. Justice in the image is drawn to people whose word matches their deed: with them there is no need to guess whether they are offended, and an agreed meeting isn’t moved at the last minute. The Hermit in the values chooses few and for a long time: two or three couples with whom you can talk about important things interest you more than a wide circle of acquaintances. And the Sun in what fills you reminds you that new people do charge you up — if meeting them gives you an experience and not just small talk.

Hence a simple landmark. You feel good with couples who can be silent with you and don’t take offence when you decline to come. It is hard where relationships are put on display or where it is customary to discuss those who are absent: Justice finds it unpleasant, and the Moon feels uneasy for a long time afterwards. If your circle has more people of the second kind than the first, it is no reason to cut ties, but it is a reason to choose consciously which meetings you spend your sunny days on.

blocks.h3: How the image and the atmosphere change over time

blocks: According to the book, a couple with Justice in its image looks each other over for a long time and takes a long time to adjust, while a couple with the Moon in its atmosphere grows together over the years and every year discovers something new in the partner. For you this means: your first years together may have been cautious, with tests and pauses, and that is the normal pace of your couple. Your closeness grows slowly but doesn’t fade. If you compare yourselves with couples who live wide open from the first month, it is easy to decide something is wrong with you. Nothing is wrong; you simply have a different pace.

One more trait of your couple can be seen only from the inside: it is hard for you to praise each other in public and easy in private. Justice doesn’t like show, the Moon guards intimacy. People close to you sometimes think you are a bit dry with each other. That is not a problem, as long as in private the warmth really is put into words and not only guessed.
If you describe your couple in one sentence for friends: outside, a clear day; inside, an evening by lamplight. The evening is good as long as faces can be seen in it.
actions: Agree that you will correct and judge each other only in private — even in small things like dates and names.
After any argument ask each other a second question — not about the matter but about the tone: “how did the way I spoke feel to you?”
If during a hard period the people close to you ask how you are, allow yourselves to answer honestly and ask for advice.

chapters.h2: What fills you and what spoils things
chapters.conclusion: You are filled by the Sun: bright shared experiences, pride in each other, each one’s growth. It also spoils things when it turns into comparison and competition. Silence restores each of you separately, while the couple is restored by light — things done and joys shared by the two of you.

cards.label: What fills you and what spoils things
cards.caption: Both upper corners are the Sun. The left one is what restores the union; the right one is what quarrels can arise over.

cards.label: Values of the couple
cards.caption: The couple’s spiritual purpose; it isn’t on the chart. The Hermit: silence and depth are what you value. But you are filled by light.

blocks.h3: Silence restores you, light restores the couple

blocks: Here your couple has a trap. You both love silence, the couple’s values are the Hermit, and it is easy to decide that rest for you means an evening at home, each in their own corner. For each of you separately this is true: Lisovskaya directly advises accepting a partner’s need to withdraw, because that is how they recover. But according to the book, the union is filled by something else. In the upper left corner, which is responsible for what nourishes the couple and holds it together, stands the Sun.

The Sun in this corner means charm, vivid impressions, a dream coming true, a partner’s growth that pushes you to grow yourself, new acquaintances, love of life, passion. All of this happens outside, in the light and together. A couple that rests only in silence gets enough sleep but doesn’t recharge: each has come back to themselves, but shared warmth hasn’t grown.

So it helps you to tell two kinds of rest apart. Personal rest is silence, a book, a walk alone, an evening without talking. It needs no justification; a warning is enough. The couple’s rest is light: a trip, a new place, a celebration, a shared victory, an evening worth remembering. It shouldn’t be waited for; it should be planned, otherwise silence will take up all your free time.

blocks.h3: What restores each of you

blocks: Lisovskaya calls the upper left corner of a personal matrix the point of inspiration. The September one has Temperance there, the February one the Hierophant, and together (14 + 5 = 19) they give the couple’s Sun. This hints at what fills each of you on your own. If that is how it is for you, the September one is inspired by measure and a calm rhythm: a day without hurry, nature and water, activities mixed in the right proportion — a little work, a little walking, a little silence. The February one is inspired by knowledge and tradition: learning from a master, reading a solid book, being where there is history, ritual, depth.

In practice it looks like this. The September one’s personal rest is a walk by the water, a sauna, slow cooking, a day off without a schedule. The February one’s personal rest is a lecture, a museum, a workshop, a long talk with someone they can learn from. The best shared sunny days combine both: a trip to an old town on a river, a workshop where a craft is taught, a hike with an overnight stay and a talk by the fire. Check whether this sounds like you — and if it does, planning rest will become easier.

blocks.h3: What fills you: rituals in the light

ul: **A sunny day once a month.** A whole day together somewhere neither of you has been: another city, an exhibition, a concert, a hike. There is one rule: the impression must be new. A favourite café is nice, but that is already cosiness, and the Sun needs novelty.

**Celebrate each other’s successes out loud.** Passed an exam, closed a project, finally fixed the tap — mark it. A small cake, a toast at dinner, a message in the middle of the day: “I’m proud of you.” The Sun feeds on recognition said in words.

**Grow side by side.** When one is learning something new, the other takes on a task too. A partner’s growth pushes you to grow yourself, and for you this is an engine: “you signed up for a course — and I’ll finally sign up for the pool.”

**People, sometimes.** The Hermit doesn’t need guests; the Sun does. Once every month or two, invite one or two couples you find interesting. You are good hosts when there are few guests and the conversation is real.

**Morning instead of evening.** In the evenings you tend to be quiet: it is a time of half-tones. Plan important joyful things for the morning and afternoon of your days off — a walk before breakfast, the market, a trip out of town. It sounds minor, but literal daylight helps this couple see each other more clearly.

**Make dreams come true in small steps.** The book directly names a dream coming true among the things that fill a couple with the Sun. Keep a list of shared “some days”, and once a season let one of them become “this Saturday”.

blocks.h3: A holiday that suits both

blocks: A holiday is where the couple’s values and what fills it clash most strongly. The Hermit in the values pulls towards silence: a cabin by the water, nobody around, books. The Sun in what fills you demands impressions: a new city, people, events. If you choose only silence, you will come back rested, but each separately. If only impressions — tired, though with photos.

Your couple suits a holiday that alternates. Two or three days of silence, when each recovers in their own way: for the September one, with Temperance in the point of inspiration, water, nature, a slow rhythm; for the February one, with the Hierophant, a place with history, a good book, an unhurried tour with a knowledgeable guide. Then one or two sunny days together: something new for both that you will have stories about afterwards. It is convenient to plan the way you have already agreed on money and decisions: one gathers the options, the other names the deadline for deciding, and the result is shared.

And a small rule for the trip itself: devote at least one evening not to impressions but to talking about how the two of you are right now. On holiday, far from everyday affairs, your couple’s Moon becomes clearer, and what stayed in semi-darkness for months at home is easier to say.

blocks.h3: What spoils things: when the Sun shines on one

blocks: The upper right corner is also the Sun, but there it is read in the minus. The book lists comparisons, arrogance, restricting the partner’s self-realisation, control disguised as care, inability to talk about problems, inflated expectations, taking credit for the partner’s victories. For your couple this is usually not loud. More like small jabs that pile up.

What it looks like for you. One gets recognition: a promotion, a successful project, praise from people whose opinion matters. In the evening the other is sincerely glad, and it charges the couple — you want to achieve something yourself, go somewhere together, celebrate. A month later there is too much of that same recognition. It is talked about at every dinner, the other answers more and more briefly, and one day it slips out: “well, you’re our star now.” The first hears envy and gets hurt. The Sun is the same, only now it shines on one.

The way out of this scene takes two. The one who is on the rise should ask about the other’s affairs themselves and help them find their own victory, even a small one. The one in the shade should say it plainly: “I’m glad for you, and it’s hard for me right now next to you.” Such a sentence removes the barb better than any self-control, because it names what the barb kept silent about.
Warning signs that the light has stopped being shared:

ul: you catch yourself thinking “at their age I had already…” or “I had that too, and more serious”;
one person’s success is discussed at home longer than the other’s joy, and the other gradually goes quiet;
one gives the other advice on how to grow — unasked, in an expert’s tone;
one person’s rest is called laziness: “lying around again?”;
one of you said in front of people “nothing would have worked without me”, even as a joke;
one has stopped talking about their affairs because “it’s not interesting anyway”.

blocks: Each such signal means one thing: the Sun is shining on one. It is better to fix it at once and in words: “Stop, I’m comparing right now. Tell me again, I just want to be happy for you.”

A separate word about control. Among the Sun’s minuses the book names control and restricting the partner’s self-realisation. In your couple it will most likely come not with shouting but through Justice: “but I can objectively see what would be better for you.” Objectivity doesn’t help here. Advice can be offered; a decision cannot be made for the other, even a very right one.

Sometimes only one of you is tired. The Sun doesn’t require both to shine at the same time: in such a period the other can be the sun for two — arrange a small celebration, drag the partner out for a walk, take over the chores. In a month you will most likely swap. The main thing is to name what is happening: “I’m worn out, be my sun for a while” sounds better than silent waiting.

blocks.h3: Why this matters for you in particular

blocks: For a couple with the Moon in the centre, the Sun is the main counterweight. The Moon makes everything hazy, the Sun makes it clear. When you are together in the light, you need to guess about each other less: you see how the other laughs, how their eyes light up, how proud of you they are. When there is little Sun, only moonlight and silence remain, and the loop from the couple’s key switches on: each in themselves, guesses grow. So a sunny day is prevention for you.

The one born in September also knows the Sun from their personal matrix: it stands in their material point. It is easier for them to notice when the light starts being shared unequally, and easier to be the first to say: “Tonight is your evening, tell me everything.” The February one, who has the Hermit in the point through which a person is easiest to influence, should know something else about themselves: they are easiest to bring out into the light through meaning. “Let’s go, it’ll be interesting to understand…” works better than “let’s go, it’ll be fun.”

And one last thing. The Sun in a couple loves generosity: gifts, surprises, a beautifully laid table. Justice loves proportion. A quarrel of “why so expensive” against “but it’s joy” is possible for you, and it is settled in advance: a line for joy in the budget, which we will come back to in the chapter on money.
actions: Put a sunny day in the calendar for the coming month: date, place, who organises it.
Agree on a stop word for comparisons, for example “sun”: whoever says it is asking simply to share their joy, without judgements.
Start a list of shared “some days” and make one of them come true each season.

chapters.h2: The couple’s money: an honest count, a dream at the entrance and change as the path to abundance
chapters.conclusion: Your money rests on clear rules and honest accounting. New money comes through a dream and talent, if they are brought to a price. Abundance grows through big shared changes that you have yet to learn to dare together. It leaks away where honesty turns into a silent count of contributions.

cards.label: Attitude to the material
cards.caption: The large circle on the right: the household, spending, savings. Justice: accounting, a plan B, decisions made together.

cards.label: Through what abundance will come
cards.caption: The middle of the couple’s money line. The Tower: big shared investments and rebuilding your way of life.

blocks.h3: Attitude to the material: rules clear to both

blocks: In the couple’s material point stands Justice. Lisovskaya describes its finances in the plus like this: official work and taxes, keeping track of income and expenses, planning ahead, big purchases decided together and calmly, there is always a plan B and a reserve. For you this comes naturally: money calms you when it is clear. You feel comfortable knowing how much there is, how much goes out and how much is set aside.

Lisovskaya reads material point C in a personal matrix as the main point of material karma — the money habits a person brings with them and needs to work on. The September one has the Sun there, the February one the Chariot. If that is how it is for you, the September one is drawn to spend on what is bright and on recognition: gifts, impressions, things that show success. The February one on movement and speed: deciding fast, taking on several things at once, taking risks. In the couple these two impulses add up to Justice: 19 + 7 = 26 → 8. Accounting and a shared agreement are needed precisely so that neither personal impulse pulls the shared money towards itself.
The couple’s material line has a continuation — a small point on the right ray, between the material point and the entrance to money. The book considers it an addition to the material point.

items.label: Attitude to the material · September one
Attitude to the material · February one

formula.caption: **5 + 20 = 25 → 7.** This point of the couple is added up from your personal points of attitude to the material: the Hierophant and Judgement. Together — the Chariot: movement and the question of who holds the reins of the budget.

blocks: In a personal matrix Lisovskaya reads this point as the attitude to the material: moods, thoughts about money, the way of influencing it. If that is how it is for you, the September one, with the Hierophant, treats money “the proper way”: by the rules, by proven schemes, with respect for how elders did it. The February one, with Judgement, sees money through family and lineage and tends from time to time to review everything anew, giving themselves and the venture a second chance. One’s rules and the other’s reviews add up to the Chariot — movement that needs a clear steering wheel.

With the Chariot in finances, Lisovskaya advises entrusting the budget to one person, otherwise a tug of war begins; in the plus she lists several projects, hard work, accounting and planning. That doesn’t mean one person has to control the money: one keeps the accounts and reminds of agreements, decisions stay shared. Which of you finds this easier — below, in the section on the budget.

The minus of Justice in money is stinginess or, on the contrary, reckless spending, secret stashes, fear of change, a situation where one doesn’t work “on principle” and the other carries everything. For you it will more likely look quieter: each silently remembers who spent how much on shared things and collects small grievances. Accounting in itself is not to blame. Trouble begins when it is kept in one’s head and not shown.

blocks.h3: Entrance to money: the Star

blocks: The entrance to the couple’s finance line is the Star, and it is reinforced: Stars also stand in both lower corners. According to the book, the lower corners in a couple are optional and weak in themselves, but if their energy is present somewhere else, they reinforce it. So the Star at the entrance to money sounds at full strength for you.

The book describes this point as the couple’s difficulties with income and how to avoid them. The Star in finances in the plus means supporting each other’s projects, earning through creativity and experience, always having a side job or a reserve, making shared wishes come true; after spending, new opportunities come. In the minus — talents go unused, chasing a beautiful life, sudden big expenses, new debts right after old ones are closed.

Your difficulties with money probably begin in one place. One or both of you has a talent people could pay for, and for years it remains a hobby. The Star loves doing things beautifully and for free, the Hermit in the couple’s task loves bringing things to perfection — together it is a recipe for an eternal “not ready yet”. The remedy is suggested by your personal entrances to money, from which this Star is made (4 + 13 = 17). The February one’s Death is the ability to declare work finished and let it go to people. The September one’s Emperor is the ability to give it a price and an order of sales. One says “done”, the other says “it costs this much”. The second difficulty is sudden spending on beautiful things: a dream trip on credit, an expensive item that is “really needed for inspiration”.

blocks.h3: Abundance: a Tower neither of you has

blocks: Lisovskaya reads through what a couple will come to abundance by the middle of the money line. You have the Tower there. Neither of you has it in your personal matrix: it is born from your identical earning Justices, 8 + 8 = 16. The path to abundance is a new experience for both, and it can only be walked together.

The Tower in finances in the plus means a shared budget and big shared investments, building or renovating together, careful treatment of things, strict discipline by rules the two of you came up with, consistency and patience. Put simply: your abundance grows in leaps, after big decisions. Moving to another city, buying a home and renovating it with your own hands, one of you changing profession with the other’s support, a shared business — each such decision breaks the usual way of life and takes you to a new level.

The minuses of the Tower in money are a sudden loss of a job or income, a change of lifestyle against your will, fear of change and a habit of expecting the worst. The book also includes here different views on money due to different levels of wealth in the parents’ families. The Tower doesn’t promise disasters. It says your growth comes through changes, and it is better to choose them yourselves than to wait for them to happen.

You have the same resources for change. Death at the February one’s entrance to money is the knowledge that money comes through the end of the old: it is easier for them to decide. The September one’s Emperor is structure and a plan: it is easier for them to lead the couple through a change without losses. One helps to jump, the other to land.

For example, the job of one of you has for years demanded more and more commuting and energy, and both have long been tired of this routine. One evening the February one says: “Let’s consider this stage over.” The September one sits down and writes out the options: move closer, change jobs, negotiate remote work — with deadlines and a reserve for the transition month. Six months later you have a different routine, more time and no less money. That is the Tower in the plus: a change you chose yourselves.

blocks.h3: The whole finance line: from a dream to an honest count

formula.caption: **17 → 16 → 8.** The couple’s finance line is read from the entrance to the crossing with relationships: a dream, change, an honest count.

blocks: Lisovskaya suggests reading the finance line both point by point and as a whole. As a whole, your line tells a simple story. Money begins with a dream and talent. The dream turns into income when you dare a big change for its sake. And the result is held by honest rules that both have agreed on. Skip the first step — and there will be nothing to change for. Skip the second — the dream will stay a dream. Skip the third — the change will eat itself, and grievances over unequal contributions will devalue what you have built.

blocks.h3: Three money scenarios for your couple

blocks: These are hypotheses, not predictions: try them on and see which is closest to you right now.

ul: **The eternal piggy bank.** Justice and the Hermit take over: you carefully save, risk nothing, keep preparing, but never dare. There is enough money, but no feeling of growth, and dreams lie for years on the “some day” list. The way out is to set a deadline for a big decision and turn the piggy bank into a “change fund” with a concrete goal.

**A leap without a map.** The Star and the Tower take over: you got inspired, decided, spent — a move, a renovation, a business — but didn’t think through rules and a reserve. Six months later you have to patch holes, and each quietly blames the other. The way out is to split big steps into stages, keep a reserve and agree in advance what each contributes.

**A strong couple.** The dream is named, the decision made together, stages and roles are clear, there is a reserve, each one’s contribution is recognised. This is how the finance line works as a whole, and your growth comes in leaps — after each big shared step.

blocks.h3: How to make a big money decision

blocks: Since abundance comes to you through big steps, it helps to have an order in which you take them. Each stage here is taken from your matrix.

ol: **Name the dream.** The Star at the entrance to money: first describe in words what you want and why — without figures and without “that’s unrealistic”. The Moon in the couple’s centre means each of you may picture the dream in your own way; check that you see the same picture.

**Give time to think — with a deadline.** The Hermit in the task and in the common language: each needs time to study the question alone. Justice asks for a deadline. Two or three weeks to study it, the date of the joint talk in the calendar.

**Write down the shares.** Justice in the material point and at the crossing of money and relationships: who contributes how much in money, time and effort, and what happens if plans change. What is written down removes future grievances in advance.
**Choose who leads.** The Chariot in the second material point: a project has one leader, the other provides oversight and support. It is good if you swap for the next big step.
**Set aside for the unexpected.** The Tower in the point of abundance: in any change something goes not according to plan. A reserve on top of the estimate is part of the decision, not a luxury.

**Celebrate the step.** The Sun in what fills you: when you finish, celebrate together. For your couple this is not a formality: this is how a big step becomes a shared victory, and the next change is easier to dare.

blocks.h3: Leaks: where it drains away

blocks: Lisovskaya calls the crossing of the money line and the relationship line the couple’s financial leaks and shows here how each one’s status and self-realisation affect the union. You have Justice there again. For you money drains away through a feeling of inequality rather than through purchases. If one earns noticeably more, or one contributes money and the other time and housework, and nobody has discussed it, both build up a feeling that it is all unfair. A sense of injustice hits the relationship harder than any expense.

formula.caption: **8 = 8.** One card in two roles: your attitude to money rests on it, and through it money also drains away when honesty stops being said out loud.

blocks: The leak is closed by the same Justice, only said out loud: agree on what counts as a contribution. Money, time, housework, caring for parents, support in a hard year — all of this is a contribution, and let it be named. Then a difference in income remains a fact and doesn’t become a grievance.

blocks.h3: Your money and relationships are linked in one point

blocks: Lisovskaya stresses that a couple’s finance line and relationship line should be read together: these areas are closely connected. Yours meet in one point, and in it stands Justice, and the middle of the relationship line is Justice too. So any money imbalance quickly becomes a relationship question for you, and any hurt in the relationship becomes a reason to recount who has put in how much. A quarrel over a renovation bill is often really a quarrel about whether each feels valued.

This link has a strong side too. When your money is in order — it is clear who contributes what, there is a reserve, agreements are kept — the relationship calms down too. A monthly money evening works for your couple as a conversation about trust, just with figures.

blocks.h3: How to set up the budget

ol: **A joint account, personal money and a change fund.** The joint account comes from Justice in the material point: everything that concerns the home is transparent to both. Personal money without reporting comes from your two Fool duals: each one’s freedom rests on an agreement, and a personal wallet is its money form. The change fund comes from the Tower in the point of abundance: it must have a named goal.

**The February one keeps the accounts, the September one plans big steps.** This division is by resources: age and gender have nothing to do with it. You both earn through Justice, but the February one also has it among their talents, so it is easier for them to turn agreements into working rules and to notice where they are broken. The September one has the Emperor at the entrance to money, so it is easier for them to build the plan of a big step: deadlines, stages, a reserve. If another way suits you better, the Chariot in the second material point asks for one thing: that each area has one person holding the reins.

**Each has their own pause.** The September one’s material point is the Sun, so they should pause before spending on bright things: gifts, impressions, things that show success. The February one’s material point is the Chariot, so they should pause before fast things: a new project, an investment, a decision made in one evening. A day’s pause on bright things for one and on urgent things for the other covers both personal impulses.

**A line for joy.** The Star at the entrance to money appears three times for you, and three Stars add up to the Lovers — those who spend on what they love (the finding about three Stars). A fixed monthly sum for beautiful and beloved things keeps this wish from breaking out in sudden purchases.

**A money evening begins with contributions.** Your money and relationships are linked in one Justice, and for you money drains away through a feeling of inequality. So once a month begin the talk about money with what each has put into the home — in money, time, care — and only then move on to figures.

actions: This week, split your money into a joint account, personal money and a change fund, and agree what share of income goes into each part.
Agree who keeps the accounts and who builds the plan of a big step; if the division by resources suits you — accounts with the February one, the plan with the September one.
Make a list of “what counts as a contribution to our home” — money, time, housework, care — and talk through how each of you values your own and the other’s contribution.
Name one big change you are saving for and the first step towards it in the next three months.

chapters.h2: Relationships and shared goals: silence, an honest word and freedom
chapters.conclusion: Your couple’s common language is an unhurried deep conversation and each one’s right to think alone. You are joined by an honest word: promises that are kept and decisions made together. You want closeness in different ways: one wants to be guessed, the other wants to be given time to think.

cards.label: Common language of the couple
cards.caption: The inner circle below the centre: the couple’s desires, agreements, common language. The Hermit: silence, depth, a space of one’s own.

cards.label: What joins you
cards.caption: The middle of the couple’s relationship line. Justice: an honest word and shared decisions.

blocks: The couple’s relationship line shows mutual understanding and respect: how the two settle questions between themselves. It runs from the point of desires and common language through the point “what joins you” to the crossing with money. For you these are the Hermit, Justice and Justice again.

formula.caption: **9 → 8 → 8.** The couple’s relationship line: from silence to an honest word, and the honest word also holds the crossing with money.

blocks.h3: Common language: silence and depth

blocks: Lisovskaya calls the inner circle below the centre the point of the couple’s shared desires, agreements and “common language”. You have the Hermit there. You understand each other best in an unhurried one-to-one conversation, without phones and without hurry. You are more interested in discussing why you act as you do than what happened during the day. Your good conversations are long and happen late in the evening, on the road, on a walk.

The Hermit in this point also sets your shared goals. Your shared desires are more about depth than speed: mastering something thoroughly, growing to mastery in your field, living the way that suits you, even if from the outside it looks strange. Your plans ripen slowly, but once ripe they hold for years.

The point stands on the line of tasks, so, as the book warns, a shared desire can also become resistance. Each wants to think on their own first, and important decisions are put off because nobody is ready to say something “raw”. The holiday isn’t booked because each is still weighing it up. The talk about the future hasn’t started because the thought hasn’t formed yet. Time passes, and there is no shared decision.

blocks.h3: How you reach agreement

blocks: Reaching agreement in two steps suits you. The first is to say the raw thought out loud without waiting for it to become a conclusion: “I don’t know yet, but I’m drawn to…”. The second is to give time to think alone and immediately set when you will come back to the talk: “let’s decide on Sunday.” The Hermit needs a pause, Justice needs a deadline. Together you get a decision that has had time to ripen and no time to overripen.

The danger is when the first step is skipped. Each thinks alone and comes with a ready decision that isn’t up for discussion. The other learns of it as a fact, and even if the decision is right, a feeling remains that they weren’t asked. Justice doesn’t forgive this: for it what was decided matters, and so does how.

An example. One of you is offered work in another city for six months. They think for a week, weigh it up, consult only themselves and come with a conclusion: “I turned it down, it’ll be better for us this way.” The other might well have agreed with this decision. But they weren’t asked, and the evening passes in polite silence. If on the very first evening they had heard “I’ve had an offer, I don’t know yet, let’s think until the weekend”, the decision would have been shared, even if it turned out the same.

blocks.h3: What joins you: an honest word

blocks: In the middle of the relationship line — the point that shows what joins the couple, which shared events and questions — you have Justice. You are joined by a promise kept. Said they would pick you up from the station — they did. Promised not to raise the subject in front of the parents — they didn’t. For you this is what romance is: a person whose word you can lean on.

formula.caption: **8 = 8.** One card in two roles on the relationship line: an honest word joins you, and through breaking it you lose the most — both trust and money.

blocks: You are also joined by shared honest causes: sorting out documents together, standing up for your rights, settling a dispute between relatives, helping someone who was treated unfairly. Among the traits of Justice in a couple, Lisovskaya also names the wish to make the relationship official. How to handle this question is for you alone to decide. If it is open for you, it is better to talk about it directly: for a couple joined by an honest word, an unspoken status of the relationship weighs more than it seems from the outside.

blocks.h3: Different desires: “guess me” and “don’t disturb me”

blocks: Here the finding about half-duals comes in handy. What each of you wants from closeness is shown by the point below the centre in the personal matrix.
